text:
Monzo’s paid plans (Extra, Perks, and Max) are only worth it if you naturally use the bundled subscriptions or insurances you would otherwise pay for out of pocket. Following Monzo's August 2026 price increases, the savings interest boosts alone require large balances to break even—especially when top UK easy-access accounts outside Monzo often pay higher rates.   
Referral Plug
+ 1

Plan Breakdown & Costs
Feature	Free (£0/mo)	Extra (£3/mo)	Perks (£9/mo)	Max (£19/mo)
Annual Cost	£0	£36	£108	£228 (£276 w/ Family)
Instant Access Savings	2.80% AER	3.15% AER	3.55% AER	3.80% AER
Select Access Savings	3.45% AER	3.45% AER	3.70% AER	3.70% AER
Money Tools	1 virtual card, 1 external bank	5 virtual cards, unlimited banks, custom categories, Google Sheets sync	Everything in Extra	Everything in Perks
Lifestyle Perks	None	None (entry to Billsback draw)	Annual Railcard, weekly Greggs, monthly Vue ticket, Uber One, YouTube Premium Lite	Everything in Perks
Insurances	None	None	None	Worldwide travel & phone insurance + RAC UK/Europe breakdown
Minimum Term	None	None	None	3 months
Verdict by Tier

Monzo Extra (£3/month — £36/year): Worth it for power budgeters. If you rely on multiple virtual cards linked to Pots to ring-fence subscriptions, want live Google Sheets exports, or track multiple bank accounts in one place, £3/month is a modest fee. However, if you just want the 0.35% Instant Access rate boost, you need roughly £10,300 saved in Monzo just to break even on the £36 fee.   
Delphina Money
+ 2

Monzo Perks (£9/month — £108/year): Worth it only if you already use at least two of the lifestyle perks. Following the price jump from £7 to £9/month, Monzo added YouTube Premium Lite (worth £7.99/month) alongside the annual Railcard (£35/year value), Uber One (£49.99/year value), monthly Vue cinema ticket, and weekly Greggs treat. Using the Railcard plus YouTube Premium Lite or a regular Greggs/Vue habit easily clears the £108 annual cost. Relying purely on the savings rate bump requires over £14,000–£21,000 in Instant Access savings to break even.   
Delphina Money
+ 2

Monzo Max (£19/month — £228/year): Worth it for frequent travellers who want bundled cover. The £10/month step up from Perks (£120/year extra) buys Zurich worldwide travel insurance, Assurant phone insurance, and RAC UK/European breakdown cover. Buying standalone annual worldwide travel insurance, gadget cover, and European breakdown cover separately typically costs £150–£250+ per year, making Max competitive—especially if you add family cover for £4/month extra. Just watch for the 3-month minimum term and check policy exclusions (like pre-existing medical conditions or gadget excess fees) before cancelling existing policies.   
Delphina Money
+ 3

The Bottom Line

Stick with Monzo Free (which already includes fee-free card spending abroad, 1 virtual card, and 3.45% AER on Select Access savings) unless you specifically want multiple virtual cards (Extra) or will actively redeem the Railcard, YouTube/Uber subscriptions, and travel insurance (Perks / Max). Also check competitors like Nationwide FlexPlus (£18/month for worldwide family travel, phone, and breakdown cover) if insurance is your main goal.
